descriptionChirho: To conceal oneself in order to attack by surprise; the basic Qal verbal action of ambushing or lying in wait for someone.
Substantive use of the Qal participle as a noun denoting the ambush itself, the ambush party, or the place of ambush.
Piel participle denoting those who set ambushes, with the intensive stem suggesting deliberate or professional ambushing.
